title: session_close tests use the canonical root, and self-exec test children stop printing into the parent suite
judge_obligation_ack: No guard logic changes: the edit rebinds a fixture path in six tests and nulls a child process's stdio; the diagnosis itself came from an independent read-only agent, and the Windows arm is judged by CI, not by the author.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee -- hooks::session_close herding::control_loop
action: Five session_close Stop tests fail on Windows only. The hook realpaths the repo root through dunce::canonicalize, and the transcript is then found by a STRING encoding of that root; the fixtures use the raw tempdir spelling, which on a Windows runner carries an 8.3 short component (RUNNER~1) that canonicalizes to a different string. The transcript is never found, so no read happens and no mark is written. Test-only: production keeps the deliberate Node-parity realpath. Rebind root to the canonical path right after the fixture in each of the five failing tests, plus stop_never_overwrites_a_live_declared_wait, which passes only vacuously today. Separately, SelfExecSpawner in control_loop.rs spawns the test binary with inherited stdio, so a deliberately failing child prints its own libtest FAILED report into the parent suite's stream. Null the child's stdout and stderr.

truths: Each rebound test resolves the same transcript path the hook resolves, on a runner whose temp path is a short name
No assertion is weakened and no test is cfg-gated away
A deliberately failing self-exec child prints nothing into the parent suite's output
